stem: A pharmacy filed a qualifying serious-event report four years ago. The underlying controlled-substance prescription is older than two years, and the manager proposes destroying every record from the case based only on the ordinary controlled-prescription retention period. What is the best response?

choices.text: Destroy everything because every pharmacy record uses the two-year controlled-prescription period.
Destroy the serious-event records because electronic filing ended the pharmacy’s retention duty.
Keep the records only until the next license renewal because renewal resets all retention periods.
Use the prescription issue date as the starting point for the five-year serious-event record period.
Keep the serious-event records; their retention period is at least five years from report filing.

explanation.core_reasoning: Different record categories have different retention rules. Even if the ordinary controlled-prescription record has passed its two-year minimum, records relating to a reportable event under 247 CMR 20.02 must remain readily retrievable for at least five years from the filing of the report.

choice_analysis.A: A two-year prescription rule does not override a longer retention rule attached to serious-event reporting records.
choice_analysis.B: Electronic submission does not eliminate preservation of the underlying report-related records.
choice_analysis.C: License renewal is not the measuring event for this record category.
choice_analysis.D: The five-year serious-event period runs from report filing rather than the original prescription date.
choice_analysis.E: At four years after filing, the serious-event record set remains inside the required five-year preservation period.

related_facts: Massachusetts controlled-substance prescriptions generally have a separate two-year retention rule.
Record-retention questions should begin by classifying the record before choosing a time period.
explanation.mpje_trap: One transaction can generate several record types; the shortest retention period does not automatically govern all of them.

reasoning_steps: Identify that the case contains more than one record category
Apply the two-year prescription rule only to the prescription category
Apply the separate five-year-from-filing rule to serious-event-related records
